source_name: Visa Inc. investor/press release hub (visa.gcs-web.com) and corporate.visa.com newsroom
why_relevant: Global/Europe Visa announcements are the channel where MK issuer wins, Visa Direct enablement and wallet launches would surface. Visa has no MK-country newsroom found; the global hub plus corporate.visa.com perspectives is the fallback entry point.

source_name: Visa product pages on MK bank sites (Stopanska Banka, NLB Banka) - Visa Direct / Visa card programmes
why_relevant: Where Visa itself is silent on MK, the issuer's own Macedonian-language product pages reveal which Visa capabilities (Visa Direct, Visa Zero, Visa Gold chatbot benefits) are actually live at which bank and when they appear - a de facto deployment tracker for scheme features.

source_name: Netcetera (G+D Netcetera) references / customer stories - Halkbank MK digital wallet
why_relevant: Explicit vendor customer page naming Halkbank AD Skopje: contactless mobile wallet, first MK wallet using CDCVM, with Mastercard MDES and Visa VTS tokenisation. Exactly the procurement-revealing artefact the cell targets.

source_name: Nextsense (Skopje) newsroom / customer announcements
why_relevant: Local MK software vendor publishing named bank deployments: article on Komercijalna Banka AD Skopje launching an online banking platform with online account opening, e-banking activation and debit card issuance. Also a Thales partner (PKI/e-signature), so it maps the digital-identity stack behind MK banks.

source_name: Entrust newsroom - card issuance / digital card customer announcements
why_relevant: Names Komercijalna Banka AD Skopje explicitly, dates the relationship back to 1995 for central card issuance, and names the local implementation partner BCS North Macedonia - simultaneously a vendor fact and a new actor (BCS) to snowball.

source_name: Asseco SEE (ASEE) case studies and news - Komercijalna banka DMS case study
why_relevant: A downloadable ASEE case study PDF on a Document Management System delivered to Komercijalna banka (project from 2010). ASEE is one of the dominant SEE banking/payments vendors, so its case-study library and news feed are a systematic route to MK bank system ownership.

source_name: Printec Group - North Macedonia country page, blog and resources
why_relevant: Self-declares presence in MK since 2006 and names Komercijalna Banka as a partner; Printec is a principal ATM/self-service/EFT-POS integrator in CEE, so its country page, blog and resources library are pointers to MK self-service estates and refresh cycles.

source_name: MK business press coverage of scheme-bank partnership announcements (mkd.mk, skopjeinfo.mk, alfa.mk, plusinfo.mk, denar.mk)
why_relevant: Scheme/bank announcements in MK are frequently distributed only through Macedonian-language media rather than the global newsroom. Confirmed items: Stopanska Banka x Mastercard expanded strategic partnership with new card products; Komercijalna Banka x Mastercard 30-year first-payment-card jubilee. These are otherwise invisible in English.

source_name: MASIT (ICT Chamber of Commerce of North Macedonia) member directory
why_relevant: Enumerates the MK technology vendor population (CaSys, Nextsense, Semos, Duna, Seavus and peers) with self-descriptions - the cheapest way to build the vendor actor map for banking/payments before hunting individual press rooms.

source_name: AmCham North Macedonia member profiles (incl. Asseco SEE)
why_relevant: Confirms local legal presence of regional banking-software vendors in MK and gives contact/scope detail; complements MASIT for foreign-owned vendors that sell into MK banks.

source_name: Halcom - banking solutions and customer references (SI vendor active in SEE)
why_relevant: Halcom is a long-standing SEE e-banking/e-signature vendor whose regional footprint frequently includes MK subsidiaries of Slovenian groups (notably the NLB network). Its solution and reference pages are a plausible route to MK deployment facts, though no MK-named reference was confirmed in this pass.

source_name: AppsRunTheWorld vendor customer databases (Temenos T24, Oracle FLEXCUBE, Diebold Nixdorf)
why_relevant: Aggregator of vendor-customer relationships; a cheap cross-check for which core-banking or self-service platform an MK bank runs when neither the bank nor the vendor issued a release. Coverage of small markets is thin and partly paywalled, so treat as a lead generator only.

source_name: BIS CPMI Red Book - Payment, clearing and settlement systems in Macedonia
why_relevant: Authoritative structural description of MK payment infrastructure (MIPS, KIBS, card processing). Dated, but it is the baseline that lets a vendor announcement be interpreted - which scheme, which rail, which operator.

source_name: Evrotrust - operator of the MK National Digital Identity Service (Mastercard ID Service)
why_relevant: Named by Mastercard as the operator of the MK national digital ID service used first by NLB Banka Skopje. As the operating vendor it is likely to publish onboarding of further MK banks - a direct read on remote-onboarding/e-signature adoption across the sector. URL inferred from the vendor name; not yet fetched.

source_name: Fintech trade press republication of scheme/vendor MK announcements (Finextra, Payments Dive, FinTech Futures, Biometric Update)
why_relevant: These outlets mirror scheme and vendor press releases and often survive after the original corporate page is reorganised or removed - a durable archive layer, and a discovery channel via their own search.

source_name: ЕСЈН — Електронски систем за јавни набавки (Public Access portal)
why_relevant: National e-procurement system of North Macedonia; the single mandatory publication point for tender notices (огласи), award decisions and contract notices by all contracting authorities. Any purchase of banking, payment, card, POS, cash-handling or e-banking services by a ministry, municipality, fund or state enterprise surfaces here with requirement, estimated value and winning bidder.

source_name: ЕСЈН — Реализирани договори (executed/realised contracts register)
why_relevant: Post-award layer of the ESJN: notifications of contracts actually executed, with realised values per contracting authority. Gives actual spend on banking/payment services rather than only the estimated tender value — the best proxy for wallet size of each incumbent bank/PSP in the public sector.

source_name: Биро за јавни набавки (BJN) — Public Procurement Bureau
why_relevant: Regulator/operator of the procurement system under the Ministry of Finance. Publishes methodology, annual reports on the procurement market, user manuals (incl. the e-Pazar electronic marketplace), lists of authorised persons for e-guarantees (a direct pointer to which banks issue electronic bid guarantees — a payments-adjacent product line), and rule changes that alter how banking services are tendered.

source_name: BJN — Овластени лица за е-гаранции (authorised issuers of electronic bid guarantees)
why_relevant: Names the banks/insurers accredited to issue electronic guarantees inside the ESJN. Reveals which financial institutions have integrated with state digital infrastructure — a leading indicator of bank-side digital capability and of the addressable market for e-guarantee tooling.

source_name: Државна комисија за жалби по јавни набавки (State Appeals Commission) — decisions
why_relevant: Publishes filed appeals daily and full decisions from its sessions. Appeals on banking/payment/IT tenders expose competitor pricing arguments, disqualification grounds, technical-spec disputes and which vendors fight for which public accounts — intelligence not present in the award notice itself.

source_name: TED — Tenders Electronic Daily (EU Official Journal supplement)
why_relevant: Above-threshold MK notices and EU/IFI-funded contracts touching MK financial infrastructure are published here, in English, with structured CPV coding and a documented API. Also captures EU-institution contracts naming MK as place of performance that never appear on the national portal.

source_name: Opentender — North Macedonia portal (Government Transparency Institute)
why_relevant: Third-party normalised and analysable mirror of MK national + TED procurement data, with buyer/supplier entity pages and indicators. Far easier to query than the ASP.NET national portal, and useful for time-series of who wins financial-services contracts. Must be treated as a derived source — completeness lags the primary portal.

source_name: OCP Data Registry — North Macedonia publication entry
why_relevant: Metadata pointer describing where MK contracting data comes from, its coverage window, format and download endpoints. Use it to decide whether bulk OCDS beats scraping, and to detect when coverage breaks.

source_name: EBRD Procurement Notices / ECEPP client e-procurement portal
why_relevant: EBRD-financed contracts in MK (financial-sector TA, FI credit lines, operational and financial performance improvement programmes for state utilities) generate general procurement notices, invitations for tenders and consultancy assignments. Donor-funded financial infrastructure work often never reaches the national portal.

source_name: World Bank — North Macedonia project documents & procurement plans (STEP)
source_subtype: IFI project document repository / procurement plan
why_relevant: Procurement plans for MK projects implemented by the Ministry of Finance — notably P176366 'Building Effective, Transparent and Accountable Public Financial Management Institutions' — list forthcoming packages (treasury/PFM IT, payment and reporting systems) with method, estimated cost and timing, months before any tender is advertised. Strongest forward-looking pipeline signal in this cell.

source_name: WBIF — Western Balkans Investment Framework tenders & opportunities
why_relevant: Aggregates EU/IFI blended-finance procurement for the Western Balkans including MK. Technical assistance packages here frequently cover financial-sector reform, PFM and digitalisation, and name the beneficiary institution.

source_name: EIB — North Macedonia country page & EIB procurement
why_relevant: EIB project pipeline for MK, including work with the National Bank and commercial banks under the Greening Financial Systems programme. Signed/appraisal-stage entries indicate where promoter-run tenders will follow; the EIB corporate procurement page covers EIB's own consultancy contracts.
